meta.application_type: Desktop application suite + CLI + shared library

findings.title: Integer Overflow in XRef Table Object Sizing
findings.description: firstObjectNumber + count arithmetic can overflow signed 64-bit integer, leading to undersized vector allocation and subsequent OOB write.
findings.exploit_scenario: Crafted PDF with INT64_MAX firstObjectNumber and count=2 causes signed overflow in desiredSize calculation.
findings.remediation: Add overflow-checked addition; validate result is positive and within reasonable bounds before resize.

findings.title: Integer Overflow in Object Stream Offset Calculation
findings.description: offset = currentOffset.getInteger() + first overflows without checking, causing parser to seek to arbitrary buffer location.
findings.exploit_scenario: Object stream with large First value plus large offset integers causes signed overflow, arbitrary memory read.
findings.remediation: Use overflow-checked addition; validate offset is within source buffer bounds.

findings.title: Unbounded Memory Allocation in XRef Table
findings.description: No maximum size limit on xref table entries vector. Attacker can trigger multi-GB allocation.
findings.exploit_scenario: PDF xref table claims 2 billion objects; application attempts massive allocation causing OOM crash.
findings.remediation: Add maximum object count limit (e.g., 10 million) and reject PDFs exceeding it.

findings.title: Unbounded Recursion in Nested Objects
findings.description: getObject() calls itself recursively for nested dicts/arrays with no depth limit.
findings.exploit_scenario: PDF with 1000+ levels of nested << /A << >> >> causes stack overflow and crash.
findings.remediation: Add recursion depth counter; throw exception at max depth (100-500).

findings.title: Integer Overflow in JBIG2 Bitmap Allocation
findings.description: width * height multiplication uses int arithmetic; can overflow when both dimensions are near MAX_BITMAP_SIZE (65536).
findings.exploit_scenario: JBIG2 segment with width=65536, height=65536 overflows int multiplication, allocating undersized buffer; pixel writes corrupt heap.
findings.remediation: Use uint64_t for product; validate product <= MAX_TOTAL_PIXELS before allocation.

findings.title: Integer Overflow in Cross-Reference Stream Loop
findings.description: Loop uses objectNumber as direct array index; if resize was undersized due to overflow in lastObjectIndex calculation, OOB write occurs.
findings.exploit_scenario: XRef stream with Index values causing overflow → undersized entries vector → loop writes beyond allocation.
findings.remediation: Add bounds check inside loop; use overflow-safe arithmetic for lastObjectIndex.

findings.title: Path Traversal in PDF Attachment Extraction
findings.description: Embedded file names from PDF used directly as output file paths without sanitization. Path traversal sequences (../) allow writing outside target directory.
findings.exploit_scenario: PDF with attachment named '../../.ssh/authorized_keys'; user runs pdfTool attachments --save-all; file written to arbitrary location.
findings.remediation: Extract only QFileInfo(filename).fileName() (basename); reject names with path separators or starting with dot.

findings.title: Signed-to-Unsigned Cast Bypass in XRef
findings.description: Negative PDFInteger cast to size_t becomes huge value, potentially bypassing bounds check.
findings.exploit_scenario: Negative object number from malformed xref → passes unsigned comparison → OOB memory access.
findings.remediation: Check objectNumber >= 0 before casting to size_t.

findings.title: Unvalidated Stream Length Allocation
findings.description: Stream Length from PDF used for allocation without maximum limit.
findings.exploit_scenario: Stream with Length=2147483647 causes 2GB allocation attempt and OOM crash.
findings.remediation: Add maximum stream length limit; validate length does not exceed remaining file size.

findings.title: Permissive Mode Suppresses Security Errors
findings.description: In permissive mode, parsing exceptions are logged as warnings and processing continues with potentially corrupt/malicious data.
findings.exploit_scenario: Malformed PDF triggers exception that would normally halt processing; permissive mode continues, allowing exploitation of subsequent parser bugs.
findings.remediation: Separate recoverable errors from security-critical validation failures; never suppress security-relevant checks regardless of permissive mode.

findings.title: Image Stride Integer Overflow
findings.description: components * width * height calculation can overflow, producing undersized pixel buffer.
findings.exploit_scenario: Image dictionary with large width/height → overflow in stride calculation → undersized allocation → heap corruption during pixel copy.
findings.remediation: Use 64-bit arithmetic; validate total allocation against maximum (e.g., 1GB) before resize.

findings.title: JPEG Row Stride Overflow
findings.description: rowStride * height multiplication can overflow in QByteArray allocation.
findings.exploit_scenario: Malicious JPEG with large dimensions → rowStride * height wraps → undersized buffer → scanline copy overflows.
findings.remediation: Check overflow before allocation: if (height > MAX_ALLOC / rowStride) reject.

findings.title: JPEG2000 Index Calculation Overflow
findings.description: y * width + x uses signed int; large dimensions cause overflow → negative index → OOB write to image component data.
findings.exploit_scenario: JPEG2000 with width=65535, height=65535 → index overflow at high y values → write before allocated buffer.
findings.remediation: Use size_t for index calculation; validate width*height fits before loop.

findings.title: Plugin Loading Without Integrity Verification
findings.description: All .dll/.so files in plugin directory are loaded without signature verification or whitelist.
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker with write access to plugin directory drops malicious DLL; loaded with app privileges on next launch.
findings.remediation: Implement plugin signature verification or maintain a hardcoded hash whitelist of allowed plugins.

findings.title: AES Padding Validation Silently Clamped
findings.description: Invalid AES padding is clamped to valid range instead of rejected, allowing modified ciphertext to be silently accepted.
findings.exploit_scenario: Attacker modifies encrypted PDF stream; invalid padding is auto-corrected rather than detected as tampering.
findings.remediation: Reject data with invalid padding bytes (< 1 or > AES_BLOCK_SIZE) by throwing exception.

findings.title: RC4 Encryption Support (Weak Crypto)
findings.description: RC4 supported for PDF revisions 2-4. RC4 is cryptographically broken.
findings.remediation: Warn users when RC4-encrypted PDFs are opened; default to AES-256 for new encryption.

findings.title: MD5 Used for Key Derivation
findings.description: MD5 used for key derivation in older revisions (2-4). R5/R6 use SHA-256+.
findings.remediation: Document as legacy limitation; ensure new PDF creation always uses R6 with SHA-256.

findings.title: Key Material Not Zeroed from Memory
findings.description: Encryption keys and passwords in QByteArray/QString not securely zeroed after use.
findings.remediation: Call OPENSSL_cleanse() on key material after use; create SecureByteArray wrapper.

findings.title: No OCSP/CRL Revocation Checking (Adobe Handler)
findings.description: Standard Adobe handler does not perform certificate revocation checking.
findings.remediation: Enable CRL/OCSP checking: X509_STORE_CTX_set_flags(ctx, X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK).

findings.title: Signature Byte Range Validation Incomplete
findings.description: Byte ranges validated for bounds but not for contiguous/complete document coverage.
findings.remediation: Warn if signed byte ranges don't cover the full document (excluding signature value).

findings.title: XXE Prevention Not Explicitly Configured in XFA Engine
findings.description: Qt QDomDocument used without explicit external entity disabling. Relies on Qt 5.15+ defaults.
findings.remediation: Explicitly disable DTD processing and external entities in QDomDocument configuration.

findings.title: XML Bomb (Billion Laughs) Not Mitigated
findings.description: No entity expansion limit or DTD rejection for XFA XML parsing.
findings.remediation: Disable DTD processing entirely or set entity expansion limit.

findings.title: CCITT Fax Decoder Bounds Check Ordering
findings.description: Array access occurs before bounds validation in Horizontal mode while loop.
findings.remediation: Check b1_index < referenceLine.size() before accessing referenceLine[b1_index].

findings.title: PowerShell Escaping Insufficient in Scanner Plugin
findings.description: Only single-quote escaping applied to paths in PowerShell script; backtick escaping not addressed.
findings.remediation: Use -EncodedCommand with Base64 or pass parameters via -ArgumentList instead of string interpolation.

findings.title: Owner/User Permission Enforcement at Crypto Layer
findings.description: Permission flags not enforced at crypto layer; relies entirely on application layer.
findings.remediation: Document that consuming code MUST enforce permissions; add runtime assertions.

findings.title: AES Zero IV for R5/R6 Decryption
findings.description: Zero IV used for AES-CBC key decryption (per PDF spec). Not a vulnerability but creates confusion.
findings.remediation: Add code comment explaining this is per PDF 2.0 spec requirement.

findings.title: PKCS#12 Default Iteration Count
findings.description: PKCS12_DEFAULT_ITER may be insufficient against modern brute-force.
findings.remediation: Use minimum 600,000 iterations per current NIST guidance.

findings.title: CI/CD Actions Pinned to Mutable Tags
findings.description: GitHub Actions pinned to major version tags (v4) not commit SHAs.
findings.remediation: Pin to full commit SHA for security-critical workflows.

findings.title: No SECURITY.md or Vulnerability Disclosure Policy
findings.description: No vulnerability disclosure mechanism or security contact found.
findings.remediation: Create SECURITY.md with responsible disclosure instructions.
